item.title: Solana Ad Lasted 10 Minutes in China. Critics Blamed CZ
item.dc:creator: Phil Haunhorst
item.description:
CZ says China pulled a Solana ad in Shanghai within 10 minutes, but did his X post trigger it? The Binance founder firmly rejects the claim.

The post Solana Ad Lasted 10 Minutes in China. Critics Blamed CZ appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Binance founder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao says a Solana (SOL) ad on Shanghai’s Bund waterfront came down within 10 minutes. He also rejected claims that his X post triggered the removal.

The Solana ad had hinted at a softer stance on crypto in China. However, organizers postponed a Solana event in the city on Friday after officers kept guests outside.

Why CZ Criticized Solana Advertisment in Shanghai

Some users on X suggested that CZ’s earlier praise for Solana’s new Shanghai office drew official attention to the campaign. His post drew more than 1 million views, carrying Solana’s China push well beyond the crypto community.

CZ disputed that link in a follow-up post. Citing details that have since emerged, he said the ad on the Bund building came down within 10 minutes.

He only came across it on X 12 to 24 hours later, in a post that still showed the Solana ad. Since China monitors speech and media in real time, censors had acted long before his post.

CZ had welcomed the office as a possible path for other blockchains. A public ad, he argued, would have signaled that China had unbanned crypto.

What the Shanghai Setback Reveals About China’s Ban

Instead, CZ conceded that “that’s not quite the case yet, it seems.” By then, officers had already stalled the Solana Shanghai event.

Mainland China has banned crypto trading since 2021. Moreover, regulators widened the crackdown in February to cover stablecoin issuance and asset tokenization.

Some market watchers see a Chinese opening as a trigger for the next Bitcoin supercycle. The swift Solana ad removal suggests that scenario remains distant.

CZ nevertheless called the campaign a good effort and urged builders to keep pushing adoption. He said he supports progress by any blockchain, from Bitcoin and BNB to XRP and SOL.

His view draws on experience. Binance launched in China in 2017, before new rules on token sales pushed the exchange offshore.

For now, the pulled Solana ad marks a setback rather than a dead end. Solana still keeps its Shanghai office. CZ, who pitches his own crypto playbook to governments, sees every such step as progress for the whole industry.

The post Solana Ad Lasted 10 Minutes in China. Critics Blamed CZ appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Did Satoshi Get Bitcoin Wrong? Claude's NSA Discovery Sparks Debate
item.dc:creator: Phil Haunhorst
item.description:
For 25 years, one suspicion haunted the mathematics protecting much of the internet: had the NSA secretly built a way to crack it? Now, an AI model may have weakened that theory. And Bitcoin’s creator is suddenly part of the argument. On Friday, Anthropic revealed that its Claude AI model solved a mystery that had

The post Did Satoshi Get Bitcoin Wrong? Claude's NSA Discovery Sparks Debate appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
For 25 years, one suspicion haunted the mathematics protecting much of the internet: had the NSA secretly built a way to crack it? Now, an AI model may have weakened that theory. And Bitcoin’s creator is suddenly part of the argument.

On Friday, Anthropic revealed that its Claude AI model solved a mystery that had baffled cryptographers for decades—in less than 30 minutes.

What Did Claude Discover About the NSA?

The controversy concerned elliptic curves, mathematical rules used to verify digital signatures without revealing private keys.

In 2000, US standards body NIST adopted several curves containing starting numbers supplied by the NSA.

Nobody explained where those numbers came from. Researchers feared the agency might have deliberately selected them to create a hidden weakness, or backdoor.

Claude traced five sets of numbers to an ordinary computer program that generated random-looking values using clock times from 1997 and 1998.

Anyone can now reproduce the results.

“In fact, this makes us more confident the curves were chosen without any backdoors or intentional weaknesses,” Anthropic said.

The finding earned a $36,864 bounty, which will go to charity.

However, questions remain about why certain numbers were skipped. The discovery makes deliberate manipulation less likely, without ruling it out completely.

Was Satoshi Wrong to Avoid the NSA Curves?

Bitcoin uses a different curve, called secp256k1. Its design uses simple, publicly understood numbers, leaving little room to conceal suspicious choices.

Satoshi Nakamoto never publicly explained why he chose it.

After Edward Snowden’s 2013 leaks exposed NSA efforts to weaken a separate encryption standard, Bitcoin’s approach gained credibility.

Ledger co-founder Nicolas Bacca reacted with “checkmate Satoshi,” arguing that the industry had avoided NSA curves in favor of a more complex alternative.

Blockstream CEO Adam Back pushed back, blaming the NSA for failing to explain its choices.

For Bitcoin holders, the practical answer is simple: nothing has changed.

Claude found no weakness in Bitcoin. Its underlying cryptography remains secure against known practical attacks.

The bigger long-term concern remains quantum computing, which could eventually threaten both Bitcoin and traditional cryptographic systems.

The post Did Satoshi Get Bitcoin Wrong? Claude's NSA Discovery Sparks Debate appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Gold Price Slides on Hot Inflation, but Schiff Says It’s a Gift
item.dc:creator: Phil Haunhorst
item.description:
The gold price slid after hot CPI, PPI and import data. See why Peter Schiff calls $4,145 gold a gift and what the Fed may do next.

The post Gold Price Slides on Hot Inflation, but Schiff Says It’s a Gift appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Gold price slid this week on hotter-than-expected US inflation data. Yet economist Peter Schiff called gold at $4,145 a gift, arguing the Federal Reserve has already lost its inflation fight.

On paper, the selloff looks backwards. Gold is a classic inflation hedge, yet three hot price reports in three days pushed it lower.

Why Peter Schiff Sees a Gift in the Gold Price Dip

The September Consumer Price Index (CPI) came first, with consumer prices up 3.7% from a year earlier. That beat the 3.6% forecast.

Wholesale inflation followed a day later. Producer prices jumped 6.3% annually, the biggest gain since 2022.

Meanwhile, import prices rose 1.1% in September, above the 0.8% consensus.

Even so, traders sold. They read the data as a signal for more Fed rate hikes, which make non-yielding gold less attractive.

The gold price slipped about 0.6% this week and has lost more than 2% over the past month. The sharpest drop came on CPI day, before prices partly recovered.

In contrast, Schiff says stubborn inflation proves Fed tightening has failed. For him, a weaker gold price marks a buying window rather than a warning.

Schiff argued gold should have soared this week, adding that traders had instead handed buyers a gift.

Can the Fed Still Win the Inflation Fight?

Markets still lean against Schiff’s view. CME FedWatch pricing implies a 90% chance of a December hike, according to Kitco.

At the same time, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh sounded upbeat on the economy this week. However, he offered no clear signal on the path of rates.

Likewise, Hamad Hussain of Capital Economics expects the gold price to drift lower through year-end as the Fed keeps raising rates. Bank of America also sees gold below $4,000 into year-end.

The pressure has already hit precious metals hard. Earlier this month, gold and silver shed $400 billion in paper value within minutes.

Silver then sank to its lowest 2026 close after the CPI release.

Ultimately, Schiff’s gold price call rests on one test. If inflation keeps beating forecasts despite higher rates, investors may start doubting the Fed rather than pricing in more hikes. That shift would favor hard assets like gold, the trade Schiff has championed for years.

The post Gold Price Slides on Hot Inflation, but Schiff Says It’s a Gift appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Apple’s First Foldable iPhone Sells Out in Minutes
item.dc:creator: Phil Haunhorst
item.description:
iPhone Duo pre-orders sold out in minutes, and online deliveries now miss Christmas. See which options holiday shoppers still have left.

The post Apple’s First Foldable iPhone Sells Out in Minutes appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Apple’s iPhone Duo pre-orders sold out within minutes on October 16, and online orders for the $1,999 foldable no longer arrive before Christmas.

That leaves holiday shoppers with fewer options. Apple’s US store now lists every model as shipping in late January.

Why iPhone Duo Pre-Orders Outran Apple’s Supply

Apple CEO John Ternus, who took over from Tim Cook on September 1, opened sales with a short teaser clip on X.

Executive chairman Cook followed minutes later, pointing buyers to the October 23 launch.

Pre-orders opened at 5 a.m. Pacific Time and sold out within minutes, Yahoo reported. Even the top $3,199 model now ships on January 22.

Apple said in a statement that pre-order demand had been “nothing short of extraordinary,” CNBC reported. The company added that it will keep accepting orders online.

However, supply looked tight well before launch. Apple pays Samsung about $250 per folding panel under an exclusive display supply deal, with no second source.

Apple unveiled the device at Ternus’s first keynote as CEO on September 9. It pairs a 5.4-inch outer screen with a 7.6-inch matte inner display.

Is a Store Visit Your Last Shot Before the Holidays?

Online buyers have little hope for December. Still, a few routes to a gift under the tree remain.

First, Apple Stores open sales on October 23, and some may have walk-in units. Inventory is expected to be very tight, and Apple has not confirmed it, according to MacRumors.

Second, buyers can try to reserve a store pickup online from October 24, when Apple’s store page says it will update availability. That may signal fresh stock reaching stores.

Finally, Apple could clear the backlog sooner than its estimates suggest. Nothing guarantees a December delivery, though.

A missed holiday window could also help rivals. Samsung says more iPhone owners are switching to its foldables.

Yet IDC analyst Nabila Popal told CNBC that Duo shipments could grow about 70% next year. That would give Apple roughly 40% of the foldable market, ahead of Samsung and Huawei.

For Apple, the iPhone Duo pre-orders show the demand is there. The harder test is getting phones to buyers before Samsung wins over the shoppers left waiting.

The post Apple’s First Foldable iPhone Sells Out in Minutes appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: White House Mocks GTA 6 After Tesla Flying Car Reveal
item.dc:creator: Phil Haunhorst
item.description:
The White House says the Tesla flying car beat GTA 6 to market, while Elon Musk now eyes a 400 mph peak for the long-delayed 2028 Roadster.

The post White House Mocks GTA 6 After Tesla Flying Car Reveal appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
The White House cheered the Tesla flying car, joking that America got it before Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6) arrived. Hours later, Elon Musk said the Roadster could reach roughly 400 mph.

The jab lands as Rockstar’s long-delayed game heads toward release. However, the car behind the joke is still at least two years away from customers.

Tesla Flying Car Turns Into a GTA Meme

The official account shared a stylized image of President Donald Trump walking past a hovering car, with Marine One overhead. The slogan “Make America Great Again” appears in the game’s signature lettering.

Trump also praised the Tesla demo. Asked by a Fox News reporter, he said he was “very happy for Elon” and called the car “very impressive.” However, he added that he did not know whether people would see him in the car.

The praise came one week after Trump handed Musk the National Medal of Science at the White House.

The administration has used pop-culture posts before, including Mario and Naruto memes that drew pushback from Japan.

Rockstar has kept its November GTA 6 launch despite years of delays. That made the Tesla flying car an easy punchline for the White House.

Can the Roadster Deliver 400 MPH Before 2028?

Tesla showed the redesigned Roadster at a SpaceX test site in Texas on October 15. Cold-gas thrusters launched the car off a ramp, and it flipped midair before landing.

Tesla also demonstrated a 0-to-60 mph sprint in under one second. At the event, Musk put the top speed of certain versions above 230 mph.

In reply to a post that cited the 230 mph figure, Musk floated a peak above half the speed of sound.

Still, buyers face a long wait. Production starts in 2028, and Tesla now lists three tiers. The base Performance version takes a $50,000 reservation, while the thruster-equipped Thrust model requires $250,000.

Only the invite-only Rocket version gets the full flight system.

Tesla first showed the Roadster prototype in 2017 and promised deliveries for 2020. By that measure, the Tesla flying car is already eight years late.

Musk also hinted at a possible Tesla SpaceX merger before the reveal. A combined company would put the Tesla flying car next to SpaceX rockets, while the White House has already made it part of its online messaging.

The post White House Mocks GTA 6 After Tesla Flying Car Reveal appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Bitcoin Bull Signals are Flashing Everywhere, Analysts Claim
item.dc:creator: Jakub Dziadkowiec
item.description:
Bitcoin bull signals flash on MVRV and MACD charts. See why PlanB, Eric Crown, and CryptoQuant data urge caution.

The post Bitcoin Bull Signals are Flashing Everywhere, Analysts Claim appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Bitcoin momentum turned positive on two widely watched indicators this week, ending a bearish stretch of roughly 10 months. PlanB, creator of the stock-to-flow model, shared the flip and questioned whether reading it could be that simple.

His doubt has a basis. BTC trades near $81,679, down 1.7% over 24 hours and below the $83,094 level shown on his chart.

Do Bitcoin Bull Signals Mark a New Cycle?

PlanB shared a chart from analytics platform Block Horizon tracking momentum in Bitcoin’s Market Value to Realized Value (MVRV) ratio. MVRV compares market capitalization with the aggregate cost basis of all coins.

Historically, green readings have lined up with bull markets and red readings with bear phases. The oscillator turned green on October 13 at +0.07, after a red run that began in late 2025.

Notably, the 2026 bear phase bottomed near -0.4. That is shallower than the roughly -0.55 troughs of 2018 and 2022.

Why a Positive Flip May Not Confirm the Bottom

Analyst Quinten Francois replied with a second gauge. Bitcoin’s weekly moving average convergence divergence (MACD) rose above zero after 44 consecutive negative weeks.

The same flip appeared in 2019 and 2023, with very different outcomes. In 2023, it preceded a rally from roughly $25,000 to above $70,000 within a year.

In 2019, however, BTC briefly climbed near $13,800 before sliding below $4,000 by March 2020. Last month, a separate 50-week moving average signal also returned after 45 weeks.

Is Bitcoin’s Four-Year Cycle Finally Broken?

Eric Crown, a member of BeInCrypto’s Market Intelligence Expert Council, argues the calendar itself has failed.

There are only 2 scenarios possible now:

1. BTC bottomed in July in which it was ahead of schedule (broken)

2. BTC bottoms anytime after today, in which it was late on its schedule (broken)

Either way, its broken… finally.

Previous lows arrived roughly a year after each cycle peak, pointing to an autumn 2026 bottom. Benjamin Cowen had expected an October cycle bottom before conceding in September that his bearish call failed.

Meanwhile, BTC dropped to $57,800 on July 1, roughly three months ahead of that schedule.

Has the Crowd Already Priced In the Bull Case?

CryptoQuant’s Analyst Consensus Index, built from votes by 164 analysts, climbed from -18.3 on July 2 to +49.2 by October 13. Over the same period, the bullish share rose from 37% to 84%.

Price has not kept pace. According to CryptoQuant’s data, BTC peaked near $87,000 in late September, and the current Bitcoin price sits about 6% lower.

On-chain momentum, price momentum, and analyst sentiment now point the same way. If halving math no longer sets the calendar, Bitcoin’s next leg may depend on whether that crowded consensus survives its first real test.

The post Bitcoin Bull Signals are Flashing Everywhere, Analysts Claim appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Former Ripple Adviser Warns XRP’s Biggest Test Is Still Ahead
item.dc:creator: Luis Blanco
item.description:
Former Ripple CBDC adviser Anthony Welfare told the AllinCrypto Podcast that the XRP Ledger (XRPL) has strong technical features. Those strengths alone will not guarantee adoption. Institutions are testing the network, and a new Nasdaq listing has put XRP in front of stock investors. What the XRP Ledger Brings to Finance The XRPL’s features suit

The post Former Ripple Adviser Warns XRP’s Biggest Test Is Still Ahead appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Former Ripple CBDC adviser Anthony Welfare told the AllinCrypto Podcast that the XRP Ledger (XRPL) has strong technical features. Those strengths alone will not guarantee adoption.

Institutions are testing the network, and a new Nasdaq listing has put XRP in front of stock investors.

What the XRP Ledger Brings to Finance

The XRPL’s features suit payments and tokenization, but Welfare argues technology is only part of the picture. Several practical questions determine whether institutions actually use it.

“When you see a lot of the things that are put out about XRP and its kind of ecosystem and Ripple as a company, and to set the stage even further there, it being this kind of like new financial system that can solve correspondent banking and that everybody can do all these use cases on and that our new financial system can run upon,” Welfare said.

Welfare’s main points are:

  • Speed, low costs, and a native decentralized exchange suit payments and tokenization well.
  • The XRP asset differs from the XRP Ledger, so institutions can use ledger functions without relying on the token.
  • Liquidity, custody, compliance, and interoperability bridge technical readiness and real-world use.
  • “The tech is there,” he said, citing his work advising central banks and on payment projects.
  • Private blockchains will likely expand first, with some activity later anchoring to public networks.

He also sees a role for auditable records that AI agents can rely on, which calls for trusted transaction layers. Stablecoins could reduce payment friction and create new orchestration opportunities for existing players, rather than eliminating them.

Is Recent Momentum Enough to Drive Adoption?

Developments over the past month lend support to that view. A European consortium is targeting euro stablecoin adoption across several networks, including the XRP Ledger.

That multi-network approach fits Welfare’s view of a multi-chain future. Welfare sees interoperability, rather than dominance by one chain, as the key commercial opportunity.

The IMF has mapped the XRP Ledger alongside other public ledgers in discussions of tokenized finance. Ripple has also expanded partnerships, including Ripple Prime services for Brevan Howard.

An integration with DriveWealth uses RLUSD on the XRP Ledger to speed up global funding. Each development shows the ledger in a different role, from settlement to funding.

Evernorth, a Ripple-backed vehicle holding about 473 million XRP, debuted on Nasdaq under the ticker XRPN this week. Shares opened at $16.68, briefly climbed to $19.38, and closed at $16.91 on Monday, October 12.

On Wednesday, October 14, XRPN closed at $15.26, down 7.40%. That gives traditional investors stock-market exposure to a large XRP treasury, without buying tokens directly.

Against that backdrop, XRP price is up 1.72% over the past 24 hours, according to BeInCrypto data. It trades near $1.34 as of mid-October, and price action remains volatile.

Even so, whether this institutional activity becomes lasting demand remains an open question.

The post Former Ripple Adviser Warns XRP’s Biggest Test Is Still Ahead appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: Raoul Pal Holds Bitcoin, Solana and Ethereum, but Calls One Wildly Undervalued
item.dc:creator: Luis Blanco
item.description:
Real Vision CEO Raoul Pal calls Ethereum wildly undervalued while still holding Bitcoin, Solana, and Sui, arguing that markets misprice blockchain networks during a podcast appearance. Still, the numbers behind his argument deserve a closer look before anyone follows his lead. Why Pal Says Ethereum Matters Most Under his stress test, Ethereum would go offline

The post Raoul Pal Holds Bitcoin, Solana and Ethereum, but Calls One Wildly Undervalued appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Real Vision CEO Raoul Pal calls Ethereum wildly undervalued while still holding Bitcoin, Solana, and Sui, arguing that markets misprice blockchain networks during a podcast appearance.

Still, the numbers behind his argument deserve a closer look before anyone follows his lead.

Why Pal Says Ethereum Matters Most

Under his stress test, Ethereum would go offline tomorrow. The outage, he says, would knock out 70% to 76% of stablecoins and a similar share of DeFi. Beyond that, most real-world assets, the digital art market and every Layer-2 network built on top would suffer too.

Taken together, Pal estimates that damage would erase between 1 trillion and $1.5 trillion. The market has not priced that risk, he argues.

“Now there is demand for Bitcoin as a collateral asset. We know that. But the convexity of, you know, something like ETH, I don’t know what the size of ETH is now, what its market cap is, but it’s wildly undervalued versus, you know, what is coming,” Pal said.

Specifically, he buys when an asset falls two standard deviations below its long-term trend, then holds. His investment approach has stayed the same for two years.

Consider 2022, when he bought Ethereum and Solana near their lows and rode them to all-time highs. Selling near the top and buying back lower, he warns, is “psychologically impossible.”

Meanwhile, he also holds Solana and Sui. Sui’s economic density, which he praises, helped it weather this year’s pullback. The same dip-buying approach extends to Zcash, as demand for privacy rises.

Why Could Liquidity Flow Back Into Crypto?

Crypto and tech, Pal argues, have lagged money-supply growth because new capital flowed into AI infrastructure. Looking ahead, rate cuts and renewed capital spending could redirect liquidity toward crypto. Crypto remains cheap against gold and the Nasdaq, he said.

Further out, he sees an “economic singularity” driven by AI agents arriving by 2030. That window, he adds, makes the next four years a critical period to build wealth.

At Sui Base Camp in Singapore, he forecast a $10 trillion crypto market within 18 to 24 months. Longer term, he says the market could reach $100 trillion by 2035.

Stablecoin supply, he expects, could reach $1 trillion within three to four years as institutions move more assets on-chain. Rising liquidity, AI investment, and tokenized assets are the key drivers.

By contrast, Bitcoin still trades below its long-term trend and looks undervalued against tech stocks. However, weak liquidity could delay a rally.

Overall, the message is consistent: focus on network value and long-term trends, not short-term noise.

The post Raoul Pal Holds Bitcoin, Solana and Ethereum, but Calls One Wildly Undervalued appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.title: JPMorgan Blocks Outside AI Agents From Customer Accounts
item.dc:creator: Luis Blanco
item.description:
JPMorgan Chase is blocking outside AI agents from logging in to or acting on customer accounts, CEO Jamie Dimon said Tuesday, citing security risks from “rogue agents.” The move puts banks and consumer AI assistants on a collision course over who controls access to financial data. BeInCrypto’s latest report on the State of AI Agent

The post JPMorgan Blocks Outside AI Agents From Customer Accounts appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
JPMorgan Chase is blocking outside AI agents from logging in to or acting on customer accounts, CEO Jamie Dimon said Tuesday, citing security risks from “rogue agents.”

The move puts banks and consumer AI assistants on a collision course over who controls access to financial data. BeInCrypto’s latest report on the State of AI Agent Payments 2026 found that agentic payments are mostly being used for microtransactions, but not within institutions at scale.

What JPMorgan Decided and Why

An AI agent is software that carries out tasks for a user, such as checking balances or booking travel.

JPMorgan see such agents as a risk when they log in with a customer’s banking credentials.

“We’re not going to allow just any outside agent to come in inside the company because that’s just too risky for clients and for JPMorgan… You don’t want rogue agents,” Dimon said during JPMorgan’s third-quarter earnings call.

Several points explain the decision:

  • JPMorgan will not let outside AI agents log in to or act on customer accounts.
  • The bank says outside agents are too risky for clients and for JPMorgan.
  • It blocks third-party agents that try to obtain customers’ banking credentials.
  • It still supports customer-authorized data sharing through open banking providers.
  • The stakes are high: $15.3 billion in third-quarter net income and $5.1 trillion in total assets as of Sept. 30.
  • A Cloud Security Alliance note says a campaign used three open-source AI agents to breach at least 27 organizations.

Together, these points explain why the bank is drawing a firm line.

Can AI Agents Still Manage Your Money?

Some firms already allow them. Germany’s Scalable Capital, for example, opened its platform to ChatGPT, Claude, and Grok in August.

Users could analyze portfolios and place trades through prompts. However, they had to approve every trade, and the assistants could not make payments or withdraw money.

Meta’s Muse follows a similar model. Launched in September, it connects to financial accounts through Plaid, offering guidance on balances, transactions, and investment holdings.

Retail is pushing back harder. On September 20, Amazon began blocking Muse from its site. As a result, shoppers who use it now see pop-ups saying the use violates Amazon’s terms.

According to Fortune, Meta declined to comment on whether Muse could keep offering financial help if more banks block outside agents. Meta is developing Poppy, a personal agent protocol with Sierra that tells companies when an agent acts for a customer.

Dimon, for his part, warned that more people relying on these agents would raise the risks for banks and customers. Still, he added that JPMorgan is building its own tools to protect customers.

The post JPMorgan Blocks Outside AI Agents From Customer Accounts appeared first on BeInCrypto.

item.content:encoded:
BTCC, the world’s longest-serving cryptocurrency exchange, has wrapped its participation in TOKEN2049 Singapore as a platinum sponsor. Over two days at Marina Bay Sands, traders, influencers and partners visited the BTCC booth and met the team.

Centered on a giant receipt installation that highlighted the exchange’s zero-fee commitment, the booth brought BTCC’s 0-Barrier Trading theme to life in Singapore.

Zero-Barrier Theme Brought to Life

Built around the 0-Barrier Trading theme, the booth showcased BTCC’s four core pillars: 0 Fees, 0 Friction, 0 Distance and 0 Panic. The receipt installation put the first of these front and center, giving visitors a hands-on look at what trading without fees looks like.

Inside the booth, the BTCC Traders Club room served as a space for more in-depth conversations. BTCC sat down for interviews with influencers and creators, covering trading, community and the road ahead for crypto.

Thousands of visitors checked in at the booth, participated in the Gold Bar Challenge and shared on social media to receive the full BTCC x AFA merch collection. 

Where Crypto Meets Football

Available exclusively at the booth, the limited-edition merch collection celebrates BTCC’s partnership with the Argentine Football Association (AFA). The six-piece collection blends crypto-native humor with football culture:

  • Crypto Bro X-ray bag: a metallic-finish piece featuring an X-ray of a crypto native’s everyday items
  • “Bear Market Survivor” selfie fan
  • “Professional Dip Buyer” cap
  • BTCC Traders Club card holder
  • Crypto meme water bottle
  • BTCC cell phone lanyard

Meaningful Conversations at The Rooftop Afters

After two days on the show floor, BTCC brought the community together on October 8 for “BTCC The Rooftop Afters,” an exclusive rooftop evening in Singapore with partners including Tencent Cloud, MegazoneCloud and BeInCrypto. 

Influencers, traders and creators came together for meaningful conversations about the road ahead for the industry and the traders who power it.

“Trade to Win” Campaign Concludes With Top Traders Rewarded

Alongside the on-site events, BTCC’s TOKEN2049 Trade to Win competition rewarded traders worldwide. Top traders were invited to join the event in Singapore, with BTCC distributing a total of $1M in rewards.

Alex Hung, Head of Operations at BTCC, commented on the event: “TOKEN2049 Singapore gave us the chance to put faces to the community we’ve been building for 15 years. It was great to meet traders in person, hear what they need and see how many of them stopped by to talk with the team. It reinforced something we believe at BTCC: trust is earned one trader at a time, through consistency, transparency and a platform that puts users first. The conversations we had in Singapore will help shape what we build next.”

During the event, BTCC also refreshed its Trust Center, where Hung shared his views on security and on 15 years of earning traders’ trust.

With TOKEN2049 Singapore now behind it, BTCC will carry its 0-Barrier Trading vision from the show floor back to the platform, with a continued focus on lower costs, easier access and trader trust.

About BTCC

Founded in 2011, BTCC is a leading global cryptocurrency exchange serving over 12 million users across 100+ countries. As the official regional sponsor of the Argentine Football Association (AFA), BTCC offers secure and accessible cryptocurrency trading services, focused on delivering a user-friendly experience while adhering to applicable regulatory standards.

X: https://x.com/BTCCexchange

item.title: Is the AI Bubble Cracking? Chip Stocks Fall for 8 Straight Days
item.dc:creator: Jakub Dziadkowiec
item.description:
Chip stocks fell 8 days straight as AI doubts and rate fears hit SOXX. See what drove it and the levels to watch next.

The post Is the AI Bubble Cracking? Chip Stocks Fall for 8 Straight Days appeared first on BeInCrypto.
item.content:encoded:
Chip stocks have closed lower for eight straight sessions, their longest losing streak in 16 years, according to Barchart. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) closed Thursday at $514.71, nearly 14% off its October high.

Thursday also brought the first sign of resistance. SOXX briefly slipped under $496, then clawed back to close above its open on the heaviest volume in months.

What Exactly Are Investors Selling?

SOXX is a $44.7 billion BlackRock fund that tracks the ICE Semiconductor Index, a basket of about 30 US-listed chipmakers. Its 10 largest positions account for roughly 62% of assets.

The biggest names took the heaviest hits. Intel has lost more than 20% in two weeks, while AMD dropped over 5% intraday on October 14.

Why Are Investors Dumping the AI Boom’s Favorite Chip Stocks?

  • AI spending doubts. OpenAI reportedly told investors its annualized revenue neared $50 billion, short of earlier $70 billion estimates. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan has also described some AI investors as gamblers.
  • Inflation and rate hikes. September consumer prices rose 3.7% year over year, topping forecasts. Traders now price a 92% chance of another Fed hike this year.
  • Asian memory rout. Selling spread from Korea’s chip-heavy KOSPI. Meanwhile, progress by Chinese memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) fueled fears that China is catching up.

Demand, however, is not the problem. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) reported a 68.7% jump in third-quarter profit, yet its US shares still fell 1.8%.

Can Buyers Defend the $500 Zone?

On the daily chart, SOXX trades below its 50-day moving average (MA), which capped rallies in August and September (red arrows). The Relative Strength Index (RSI), a momentum gauge, has fallen to 36, its lowest reading since July.

Thursday’s volume spike suggests dip buyers are stepping in. If selling resumes, the 0.5 Fibonacci retracement near $481 is the next major support.

Overhead, SOXX must reclaim $523 and the 50-day MA near $540. The bigger barrier sits at $573, the 0.236 Fibonacci level.

UBS reads the sell-off as a reset:

“More of a recalibration of expectations than a fundamental break in the AI investment story.”

JPMorgan strategists also flagged a possible inflection point. Yet Big Tech plans roughly $800 billion in capital spending this year, per Goldman Sachs. The next leg for chips may hinge on borrowing costs, not demand.

item.content:encoded:
Japan’s three megabanks, Mizuho, MUFG and SMBC, announced on October 16 that they completed a joint yen stablecoin pilot for cross-border payments, conducted in July.

The test points to a new model for bank-issued digital money, with real transactions targeted for fiscal 2026.

How the Yen Stablecoin Pilot Worked

Three major Japanese megabanks and two partners took part in the pilot project. The banks issued one shared yen token, which the group tested end to end.

The partners split the work across issuance, custody, and technology, and each firm was responsible for its own part of the process.

  • The three participating megabanks conducted the pilot from July 17 to 23, 2026.
  • Mitsubishi UFJ Trust and Banking acted as trustee, while technology firm TISI Inc. joined as the technology provider.
  • The tokens were issued under Japan’s Payment Services Act, and the three banks acted as joint settlors.
  • Circulation was limited to KYC-verified users at participating banks and had no cap, while bank deposits backed the tokens.

A trustee holds assets for others and must follow the trust’s terms. Trustees must act in the interest of beneficiaries. Beneficiaries are the people who hold rights under the trust.

Settlors create a trust and place assets into it. KYC, or know-your-customer, means banks verify each user’s identity before granting access.

What Did Japan’s Pilot Actually Prove?

The pilot’s main use case was cross-border settlement between Japanese headquarters and the overseas offices of Mitsubishi Corporation.

Cross-border settlement means finalizing payments between parties in different countries. Redemption means returning tokens for cash. The pilot verified the full cycle: issuance, transfer, and redemption.

Results confirmed the safety, reliability, and operational viability of joint issuance. Participants gained practical insight into systems and operations. Compliance work also covered anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing measures.

Subscribe to our YouTube channel to watch leaders and journalists provide expert insights.

Those findings matter because the banks had not yet run any live transactions. For the wider industry, the result is a workable template for banks exploring digital money. Live transactions remain the next milestone for the project.

The Financial Services Agency-backed project was selected in November 2025 under its FinTech PoC Hub and Payment Innovation Project. SMBC provided the blockchain platform, which TISI built.

In June, the banks announced a joint council to study governance and operations. Fiscal 2026, the target year for real transactions, runs from April 2026 to March 2027.
